note: Written after recovering the wall text from tools/l6.py, which is where this lesson's teaching had been kept only as pixels. Checked against the recovered walls, the worksheet's exam practice and the activities, station by station.
lesson_fields_note: The starter, key question and key vocabulary below are authored. This lesson's worksheet predates tools/wsspecs and never carried them, so there was nothing to recover: the lesson plan was printing 'not in the lesson record' where a teacher needs a retrieval question. Each starter retrieves the lesson before this one rather than previewing today's answer, and none of them is on the pupil's sheet, so they go on the board.

lesson_fields.starter: From last lesson, without notes: what is the internet, in one sentence? And what does a DNS server do when you type an address into a browser?
lesson_fields.keyq: Which shape of network would you fit here, and what are you giving up by choosing it?

nw-l06-o1.note: No exam item on this sheet asks 'what is a star network' on its own, which is right: at GCSE the definition is only ever worth having inside a judgement. It is checked by the two station activities and then has to be used in x4.

nw-l06-o2.note: Full mesh, its trade-offs, and the wireless case. Wireless mesh is taught at s9 and assessed nowhere on paper; from October 2026 it is at least applied, in the scenario sort at the final station.

nw-l06-o3.note: One station, two activities, no exam item. Until October 2026 this outcome could not be traced at all, because the only place the lesson said it was the painted wall. The wall says it clearly; the gap was in what could be read, not in what was taught.

nw-l06-o4.note: The lesson's real outcome, and the one the four-mark question rests on. s10 now runs in two steps: sort statements to the topology they describe, then choose a topology for six places it has not seen. The second is the rehearsal for x4.

for the owner: Station 5 of each part - 'Break it!' and 'Star vs mesh' - is a hand-drawn panel rather than a station card, so its wall text could not be recovered and the lesson plan lists stations 1-4 and 6-9. That is the same shape as every other lesson in the course, whose final challenge station has no wall list either, so nothing was changed for it.

This lesson has no key question, no starter and no key vocabulary in any form the build can read, because its worksheet predates tools/wsspecs and survives only as a built .docx. The lesson plan says so on the printout rather than inventing them. Recovering those three is a worksheet-side job, not a lesson-side one, and was left alone here.
